title: The Unexpected Garden
premise: Cyrus Villalobos has built a career on erasure: as a ghostwriter, he pens other people's truths while burying his own—including a past love he abandoned to save his family from ruin. Hired secretly to ghostwrite the memoirs of rival writer Julian Marsh, he returns to his hometown vineyard for a family reunion and recruits Marisol Reyes, the woman he once loved and who now runs her late father's winery, to pose as his girlfriend. The fake romance turns real just as Cyrus discovers Julian's memoir will expose the Villalobos family secret that destroyed both their fathers' friendship—and that Marisol is the one person with the power to confirm or deny it. When she learns Cyrus has been writing the book that could take her vineyard, their fragile trust shatters. At the first harvest, Cyrus must publicly claim authorship of his own life—burning the manuscript, confessing everything, and choosing Marisol over the career that once saved him.
about_author: Edmund Eriksen is the pen name of a former wine-country journalist who spent a decade covering vineyard families before turning to fiction. He writes about memory, inheritance, and the stories we tell to survive our own histories.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Manuscript
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. In his New York apartment, Cyrus finishes ghostwriting a celebrity memoir and receives the lucrative offer to write Julian Marsh's—the rival whose fame eclipsed his own abandoned novel. The invitation to his family's vineyard reunion arrives the same day. Emotional beat: the hollow comfort of being unseen, and dread at going home.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Back in wine country, Cyrus's mother announces she's invited everyone—including Marisol Reyes, his ex, now running her father's winery. Panicked, Cyrus asks Marisol to pretend they're together again, framing it as mutual PR against gossiping neighbors. She agrees, coolly, with conditions. Emotional beat: nervous negotiation masking old wounds.

chapters.title: Rehearsal
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. They rehearse their couple story over wine in her cellar, trading half-truths. Marisol reveals fragments of her father's decline and the vineyard's financial peril; Cyrus conceals the Marsh contract. A shared laugh over an old memory cracks something open. Emotional beat: guarded tenderness, the danger of almost-honesty.

chapters.title: The Reunion
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. The reunion unfolds in staged intimacy—shared toasts, his aunt's knowing looks, Marisol's hand finding his too naturally. By dessert, a toast about 'second harvests' lands like a confession, and Cyrus realizes the performance has stopped being one. Emotional beat: the vertigo of real feeling inside a lie.

chapters.title: What the Vines Remember
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Walking the old rows at dusk, Marisol and Cyrus finally speak of why they ended—his father's bankruptcy, her father's silence, the letter Cyrus never sent. She shows him her father's old journals, which mention a disputed parcel of land. Emotional beat: grief shared becomes intimacy; the past tense begins to wobble.

chapters.title: The Other Man's Truth
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Interviewing Julian by phone, Cyrus hears the memoir's centerpiece: Julian claims the Villalobos family cheated his father out of the parcel that is now Marisol's best vineyard block—and he wants Cyrus to verify it. Cyrus realizes Marisol's journals are evidence either way. Emotional beat: the trap closing; corruption dressed as justice.

chapters.title: Harvest Eve
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. On the eve of first harvest, Marisol finds a draft chapter of the Marsh memoir on Cyrus's laptop—her family named, her land at stake. Confronted, Cyrus can only stammer explanations. She sends him away. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding old abandonment; identity collapsing into the ghost he always feared he was.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ink
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV. Cyrus confronts Julian, discovering Julian manufactured the land-grab story to destroy the Reyes winery and buy it cheap—a vendetta built on his father's bitterness. Julian offers Cyrus co-authorship and redemption-by-association if he confirms it. Emotional beat: Cyrus sees power's corruption clearly and refuses, burning the manuscript.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Cyrus's POV, then Marisol's. At dawn on harvest day, Cyrus arrives uninvited, publicly confesses everything—to Marisol, her workers, his own family—and hands her his true novel, written years ago, about them. Marisol reads it among the vines as pickers work around them. Emotional beat: vulnerability as courage; authorship reclaimed.

chapters.title: The Unexpected Garden
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Weeks later, the memoir scandal breaks without Cyrus—he's credited nowhere, and doesn't mind. Marisol's harvest is the finest in a decade; the disputed parcel stays hers. In the overgrown garden between their two properties, they plant something new together. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—love in present tense, identity rooted at last.
